02_dashboards/sales/ISZE_AIM_Classificat.title: The parts classification model — how it works, how accurate it is, and how it compares
firstLines: OBSERVED Classification of billed / listed part numbers
PURPOSE Family language for commercial analysis — not a revenue gap model
FLEET Historical only where fleet appears
ISUZU EUROPE · AFTERSALES ANALYTICS · INTERNAL WORKING PAPER
How we sort 165,000 parts — identity on the truck, competition beside it

The parts classification behind our pricing and category reporting assigns every part three labels from its price-list description. This paper explains how that model works, how it checks against customs codes and Isuzu’s own figure numbers, why one fused label cannot carry both what a part is and how it competes, and how the locked two-axis design compares with Volvo, Isuzu’s catalogue, and the standards the aftermarket actually runs on.

02_dashboards/pricing/ISZE_Pricing_Revis.title: Price revision - distributor, family and source of supply
firstLines: Where the parts price revision lands

By distributor, by AIM family at all three levels, and by source of supply: Japan through IML or Thailand through IMIT. Parts billed 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2026. Opens from Explorer with no server and no internet — the data and charts are inside the file. Built 2026-09-24. Network tie-out: step €1,652,141, weighted 5.96%, both checked against the published revision.

What the headline is. The percentage is a base-price move: the euro increase measured against the prior base price, weighted by the quantities actually billed. It is not a revenue, margin or elasticity outcome, and no demand response is modelled. Parts billed euro covers every in-scope line; the weighted percentage covers only lines priced on both sides, which is stated on every panel.

02_dashboards/pricing/ISZE_Pricing_Revis.title: Price revision + Japan FOB exchange rate (01/10/2026)
firstLines: Price revision + Japan FOB exchange rate

Official exchange rate for Japan-sourced spare parts from Isuzu Motors Limited: 178.5 JPY per EUR, effective 1 October 2026 to 31 March 2027 (Suzuki san mail, September 2026). The AIM L3→PN revision pack stays as a separate frozen file. This page only adds the purchase-side effect: we buy Japan parts cheaper in euro.
What changes. The selling-side list step is still €1.65M (5.07% on billed). That number does not move with FX — it is the JPY base-price revision converted at the model rate.

What the new rate does. Japan FOB in euro falls by 3.31% (172.6 → 178.5). This is a purchase-side figure for Japan-sourced parts only. It is not the published list move and must not be read as one: the published move is +1.8001% on the whole priced book and +5.7369% on Japan, and it is a ratio of two prices read from the price list, so no historical exchange rate is an input to it. On the same billed quantities, that is €266k less purchase cost at the prior base price, or €283k if you reprice FOB on the new base price. Thailand is unchanged — Suzuki’s rate is Japan-sourced only.
Thailand FOB stays on 172.6. Lines with no source label are left on the baseline rate. Sibling frozen pack: ISZE_Pricing_Revision_AIM_Source_L3PN_20260918.html.
